ruling.recommended_action: Reject the fare protest; note the metered difference is attributable to the accident-related diversion (LTA incident 08:44 on Tampines Expressway, band 1), no refund due.

segment_findings.reason: Crawl at ~8 km/h 08:59:50–09:03:20 on a straight axis off the route polyline, rejoining the expressway at ~(1.3866,103.9140); ~0.8–1.0 km on the local-road approach. No traffic incident (the LTA Accident is plotted further east at 1.38075,103.91929 on Tampines Expressway, RD-4) and no chat agreement (RD-5, chat contains only pickup messages), so it is not exempt under RD-4/RD-5 — but its extra km cannot be isolated under RD-2 because segment seg2 is exempt and the remaining gap is within the ~0.25 km map-matching residual plus thinned-trace error.

Driver travelled NE 09:03:50–09:07:20 to ~(1.3885,103.9237) and looped back to (1.3845,103.9192), avoiding the optimal-route stretch of TAMPINES EXPRESSWAY that carries the 08:44 LTA Accident 'lanes blocked' at (1.38075,103.91929) — on-route within the 300 m match radius, reported before the segment began and live in the window, plus band 1 (0<9 km/h, SYN-1005, 08:46:20–09:04:00): exempt under RD-4(a) (RD-4(b) band only corroborates), so no extra-km refund under RD-2.

rejected_claims.reason: Rider says the meter exceeded the estimate and no route change was agreed. The only well-established off-route stretch is the Tampines Expressway diversion (seg2), which is exempt under RD-4(a) because the LTA-recorded 08:44 accident blocked lanes on the replaced optimal route (band 1 corroborates); no consent was needed for a reasonable-cause diversion. Under RD-2 the refundable extra km is 0, so the metered fare of $27.27 stands.
